entities.summary: The Sopot culture is a Neolithic archaeological culture that was first identified in eastern Slavonia in modern-day Croatia, and was since also found in several sites in Hungary. It was a continuation of the Starčevo culture and strongly influenced by the Vinča culture. Some of the archeological sites where artifacts of it were found include Samatovci, Vinkovci–Sopot, Otok, Privlaka, Vinkovci–Ervenica, Osijek, Bapska, Županja, Klokočevik. It spread into northern Bosnia from its original area to the west to northwestern Croatia and to the north to Hungarian Transdanubia, where it helped Lengyel culture start.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Sopot culture played a significant role in shaping the Neolithic period in Eastern Europe, influencing the development of subsequent cultures such as the Lengyel culture. Its spread across the region helped to establish trade and cultural exchange networks.
